title: Buttonholes and Simple Closures
description: Add buttons, loops, ties, and simple closures so projects stay shut and feel finished.

content.summary: Closures can be as simple as a chain loop, a buttonhole space, or a tie that matches the project.
content.whyItMatters: A practical closure improves function and gives pouches, sleeves, and cases a more polished result.
steps: Choose a closure that suits the fabric thickness and how often the item will be opened.
Measure the button or opening before making the loop or buttonhole.
Crochet the closure neatly so it sits flat and does not pull the fabric out of shape.
Sew buttons on securely and test them before finishing the project.
Open and close the piece a few times to make sure the closure is comfortable to use.
content.practice: Add one chain-loop closure and one buttonhole closure to two small swatches.
commonMistakes: Making the loop too loose so the button slips out.
Placing the closure off-center so the flap twists.
